response.title: Finding a Safe Place by the Creek
response.passage:
The environmental club planned to measure water movement in a creek before choosing a site for a cleanup. After a night of rain, the creek looked calm from the bank, but its surface told only part of the story. Ms. Chen brought a reliable flow meter, whose measurements had matched a professional team's during last year's survey. Its digital display showed how quickly the water moved past a point.

At the first bend, two readings differed sharply, even though the students had held the meter at the same depth. The group did not accept either number as correct without checking the equipment. They repeated the test with a second meter and found that its sensor was loose. Once they had a dependable reading, Ms. Chen showed them how to compare speeds at different points. The current was strongest near the narrow center of the creek and slower beside the bank.

That steady movement carried floating leaves toward a quiet pocket below the footbridge. Since the club wanted volunteers to work safely, the students chose that sheltered bank as their meeting point. They marked the spot with orange tape and sent its location to the school office. On cleanup day, everyone gathered there, and the earlier measurements helped them keep the group away from the faster water.

response.extraOption: The club poured cooking oil into the creek so the students could see which way the water moved.
